verses.text: So you have no excuse, whoever you are when you judge someone else. When you judge them, you condemn yourself, because you who judge do the same things.
We know God's judgment against people who do such things is based on the truth.
Do you really think you will escape God's judgment, even though you judge people who do these things while doing them yourself?
Or do you look down on God's rich kindness, restraint, and patience? Don't you see that God's kindness is meant to lead you to turn back to him?
But because your heart is stubborn and won't turn back, you're storing up judgment for yourself on the day when God's righteous judgment is revealed.
God ‘will repay each person according to what they have done.’
To those who keep doing good and seek glory, honor, and immortality, he will give eternal life.
But to those who are self-centered, reject the truth, and follow wrongdoing, there will be anger and fury.
There will be trouble and distress for every person who does evil—for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.
But glory, honor, and peace will come to everyone who does good—for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.
God doesn't play favorites.
Everyone who sinned without the law will perish without the law, and everyone who sinned under the law will be judged by the law.
It's not the people who hear the law who are right with God. The ones who do what the law says will be declared right.
(When Gentiles who don't have the law naturally do what the law requires, they become a law to themselves, even though they don't have the law.
They show that what the law requires is written on their hearts. Their conscience confirms it, and their thoughts sometimes accuse them and sometimes defend them.)
This will happen on the day God judges people's hidden lives through Jesus Christ, according to the Good News I proclaim.
Now, if you call yourself a Jew, rely on the law, and take pride in God,
if you know his will and can recognize what matters because you've been taught from the law,
if you're sure you can guide the blind and be a light for people in the dark,
correct the foolish, teach the young, and claim to have the pattern of knowledge and truth in the law—
then you who teach others, don't you teach yourself? You preach against stealing, but do you steal?
You say people must not commit adultery, but do you commit adultery? You hate idols, but do you rob temples?
You take pride in the law, but do you dishonor God by breaking it?
As Scripture says, ‘God's name is insulted among the Gentiles because of you.’
Circumcision is valuable if you obey the law. But if you break the law, your circumcision counts for nothing.
So if someone uncircumcised keeps the law's requirements, won't God count that person as circumcised?
Won't the one who is physically uncircumcised but obeys the law condemn you, who have the written law and circumcision but break the law?
A person isn't a Jew just because of outward appearance, and circumcision isn't only an outward mark on the body.
A Jew is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, brought about by the Spirit, not by a written code. That person's praise comes from God, not people.
